candidates.tagline: Apple spent 6 years on a foldable iPhone and it still has a crease
candidates.story: Apple announced the iPhone Duo on September 9, 2026 — a $1,999–$3,199 foldable that Apple describes as having a display that is 'wonderfully flat and smooth,' while every hands-on review published the same day confirmed the crease is still clearly visible, and Apple refused to disclose how many fold cycles the hinge is rated for.
candidates.why_funny: Apple's entire marketing pitch is that the fold is invisible, and the nano-texture exists specifically to minimize the crease they won't admit exists.
candidates.alt: The Apple iPhone Duo open, showing its 7.6-inch inner foldable display with the fold line running down the center of the screen

candidates.tagline: She got zero points, broke a sport, and Netflix gave her a documentary.
candidates.story: Netflix released 'Untold Raygun: Breaking Badly' on September 1, 2026 — a full-length documentary about Australian breakdancer Rachael Gunn, who scored zero points in all three rounds of her Paris 2024 Olympic debut and whose performance contributed to breaking being dropped from the 2028 Games; critics called the documentary 'more infuriating than the performance itself.'
candidates.why_funny: The logical response to embarrassing an entire sport off the Olympic program is apparently a Netflix documentary asking you to feel bad about it.
candidates.alt: Rachael 'Raygun' Gunn mid-performance, posed in her signature kangaroo-hop stance under dramatic blue stage lighting
